title: Birth and first piano lessons
summary: Carter was born in New York in 1907 and had piano lessons from his mother, his sister and a teacher at about age 10-11.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: PROCEEDINGS
This is an interview with Benny Carter, conducted by Marl Berger as part of the oral jazz history program of the Smithsonian Institution. We are in Princeton, and this is October 13, 1976.
Benny, to begin at the beginning, let's just ask where and when you were born.
I was born in New York City on August 8, 1907.
How did you feel?
I felt pretty good at the time!
Okay.
But I feel much better now.
All right. When did you begin to get interested in music as nearly as you can remember?

Well, as nearly as I can remember, it must have been about at the age of 10. And my mother played piano, not professionally, of course -- but she played in church occasionally, and she gave me some piano lessons at home.

And following that, my sister -- who had been studying piano -- she gave me some piano lessons. And following that when she could stand me no longer, I took some lessons from the teacher from whom she had been taught.
Do you remember that her teacher's name?
No, I don't.
That was a piano teacher.
Yes.
And that must have been -- when? About 1917 when you were about 10, or maybe a little bit later?
Well, about ten. Well, Actually, when I went to the piano teacher, it was about a year later.
So it was about 1918.
When you were about 11.
Yes, something like that, yes.
